title: WEP died because its 24-bit IVs repeated by lunch
body: WEP encrypted each packet with RC4 keyed by a shared secret plus a 24-bit initialisation vector sent in clear. On a busy network those IVs exhausted and repeated within hours, and weak-IV analysis recovered the key from passively sniffed traffic. AirSnort made it a download in 2001. The cipher's core was fine; the key scheduling was a revolving door.
source_hint: Fluhrer, Mantin, Shamir (2001), RC4 key scheduling attack
